report.summary: Both books UI tests fail at the same step: the page object clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"), but the books page's button is data-testid="add-book", so the locator never matches and Playwright times out after 5s. This is a test bug in tests/support/pages.py:44, not an app regression. Fix the test id there first, which should clear both failures.

causes.title: Page object uses a test id that doesn't exist on the books page
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add() clicks the element with data-testid "add-books" (plural), but the Add button in app/templates/books.html is "add-book" (singular). The locator never matches, so Playwright waits the full 5000 ms and raises TimeoutError before any app behavior is exercised. Both failing tests call BooksPage.add() first, so both fail at this line. The other ids used by the page object (title, author, year, book-row, error, etc.) match the template, so this looks like a one-off typo rather than a systematic naming change. Neither test reached any assertion, so their real expectations are unverified.
evidence: Call log: "waiting for get_by_test_id(\"add-books\")" in both failures (tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:13 and :42, via tests\support\pages.py:44)
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:45 uses get_by_test_id("title"), which matches books.html:6, so the rest of the page-object ids are consistent with the template
causes.suggested_fix: Change tests/support/pages.py:44 to self.page.get_by_test_id("add-book").click(). Then rerun tests/ui/test_books_ui.py. Also consider a short test that checks the add button's test id exists so this doesn't silently regress. Once the click works, check that the future-year test's assertions (error shown, title input kept) still hold, since they have never run against this build.
